# Atlas of slices — what the mass table says, with no model

*Generated by `models/atlas/atlas.py` from AME2020 measured binding energies (2550 nuclides). No fitted number and no mechanism anywhere in this file. Every table is a slice the answer must pass (SPEC v6 §2). Half-lives are not used: the half-life table is not in `data/`.*

## 1. Even beats odd

For each nuclide with a measured neighbour on both sides: is it more bound (even count) or less bound (odd count) than the mean of its two neighbours? `gap` > 0 means the rule holds.

| count | nuclides | rule holds | exceptions | mean gap (MeV) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| neutron number | 2264 | 2259 | 5 | 1.11 |
| proton number | 2173 | 2166 | 7 | 1.27 |

## 3. The gain from adding one alpha

Gain = BE(Z+2, N+2) − BE(Z, N) − BE(⁴He). Along N = Z (the alpha ladder), then the same quantity for every even-even nuclide, averaged by how far the *product* sits past a closed number.

| step | gain (MeV) |
|---|---|
| He-4 → Be-8 | -0.09 |
| Be-8 → C-12 | 7.37 |
| C-12 → O-16 | 7.16 |
| O-16 → Ne-20 | 4.73 |
| Ne-20 → Mg-24 | 9.32 |
| Mg-24 → Si-28 | 9.98 |
| Si-28 → S-32 | 6.95 |
| S-32 → Ar-36 | 6.64 |
| Ar-36 → Ca-40 | 7.04 |
| Ca-40 → Ti-44 | 5.13 |
| Ti-44 → Cr-48 | 7.70 |
| Cr-48 → Fe-52 | 7.94 |
| Fe-52 → Ni-56 | 8.00 |
| Ni-56 → Zn-60 | 2.69 |
| Zn-60 → Ge-64 | 2.57 |

**All even-even nuclides: mean alpha gain by where the product's neutron number sits relative to a closed number** (products with 8 ≤ Z):

| product N relative to closed number | mean gain (MeV) | nuclides |
|---|---|---|
| -4 | 4.85 | 41 |
| -2 | 5.07 | 43 |
| +0 | 4.99 | 46 |
| +2 | 2.72 | 47 |
| +4 | 2.71 | 50 |
| +6 | 3.31 | 49 |

| product Z relative to closed number | mean gain (MeV) | nuclides |

## 6. Exits

For every measured nuclide whose neighbours are also measured (`unknown` otherwise): which ways out are open on energy alone — beta-minus, electron capture, alpha, one neutron, one proton. A nuclide with no exit open cannot decay by any of these. One with an exit open that is nonetheless found in nature is holding a lock against an available way out; those are slices of the second kind (SPEC v6 P14).

| exits open | nuclides |
|---|---|
| 0 | 191 |
| 1 | 975 |
| 2 | 763 |
| 3 | 61 |
| unknown | 560 |

**No exit open: 191 nuclides.** By mass number: 64 up to A = 60, 115 from 61 to 140, 12 above 140.

Heaviest with no exit: Dy-164, Dy-163, Gd-160, Tb-159, Gd-158, Gd-157, Gd-156, Sm-154.

**Alpha is the only exit open: 132 nuclides.** These are beta-stable but could shed an alpha on energy alone. The lightest: Be-8 (0.09 MeV), Ce-142 (1.30 MeV), Nd-143 (0.53 MeV), Nd-144 (1.90 MeV), Nd-145 (1.57 MeV), Nd-146 (1.18 MeV), Sm-146 (2.53 MeV), Sm-147 (2.31 MeV), Nd-148 (0.60 MeV), Sm-148 (1.99 MeV), Sm-149 (1.87 MeV), Sm-150 (1.45 MeV).

Even-odd make-up of the no-exit set:

| Z | N | nuclides |
|---|---|---|
| even | even | 114 |
| even | odd | 36 |
| odd | even | 37 |
| odd | odd | 4 (H-2, Li-6, B-10, N-14) |
